events.title: French Saint-Domingue plantation colony
hints: Once the richest colony in the world, its sugar and coffee were produced by enslaved people.
A revolt that began in 1791 ended colonial rule and created the first Black-led republic.
events.summary: France acquired the western third of Hispaniola in 1697 and built Saint-Domingue into the world's leading sugar and coffee producer through the labour of several hundred thousand enslaved Africans. The Haitian Revolution (1791 to 1804) ended slavery and French rule.

events.title: Independence debt to France
hints: Recognition came at the price of a huge indemnity paid to the former colonial power.
The payments, and the loans taken to make them, lasted well over a century.
events.summary: In 1825 a French fleet backed a demand for 150 million francs (later reduced to 90 million) as the price of recognising independence. Loans taken to pay the indemnity kept the country in debt to French banks until 1947.
events.quip: Possibly history's most audacious invoice: payment for the privilege of having won.

events.title: United States occupation of Haiti
hints: Marines landed in 1915 and stayed for nearly two decades.
Customs revenue was controlled by the occupier, and a forced-labour road gang system was revived.
events.summary: US Marines occupied the country from 1915 to 1934. Washington controlled customs and finances, rewrote the constitution to allow foreign land ownership, and the forced-labour corvée system for road building sparked a revolt in 1919.

events.title: Spanish conquest of Hispaniola
hints: A fort built from the timbers of a wrecked flagship in December 1492 was the first European settlement in the Americas.
The Taíno population was devastated by forced labour in gold fields and by disease.
Spain formally ceded the western part of the island to France at the 1697 Treaty of Ryswick.
events.summary: After Columbus's flagship was wrecked on the north coast in 1492, Spain established the first European settlements on the island. Taíno communities were forced into the encomienda labour system and decimated by labour, violence and disease. Spain ceded the western third to France in 1697.

events.title: US financial control and the Banque Nationale
hints: A New York bank gained control of the national bank in 1910 and helped arrange a 1914 transfer of its gold reserve overseas.
The 1915 treaty gave Washington control of customs and finances for twenty years.
Fiscal supervision outlasted the military occupation and ended only in 1947.
events.summary: From 1910 National City Bank of New York took a stake in the Banque Nationale, and in December 1914 US Marines removed gold from its vaults to New York. The 1915 treaty placed customs and finances under US control, with supervision continuing until 1947.
